criteria.rationale: Examined the spec's assumptions against evidence: memo soundness rests on closeoutChain being consulted only in localScopeClosed (verified by grep, closeout_review_policy.go:393); remote proofs being conservatively cut is verified by TestDoctorCloseoutMemoForeignSpecProofIsNotRetained; the F5 timing claims are recorded measurements in .pose/reports (not reproduced, treated as reported facts); R1-F1/R1-F2 are correctly kept as accepted-risk follow-ups. The one unverified claim (surface-check passed) is contradicted, see N1.
Memo/trace mutexes, no lock held over recursion, defer-closed memo; focused tests pass under -race at a5c43041.
No exported API, JSON or CLI/MCP shape changed; new fields and the listing hook are unexported.
Errors, false results and cuts are never cached; query error then audit error take precedence and no list is published.
Snapshots allocated after the read view and before binding in both operation entries; remote crossings unmemoized; doctor consumer unchanged.
Audit/binding failures surface as doctor closeout-review.owed warnings with error text and remediation (internal/cli/doctor.go:1616-1619).

Examined the public CloseoutReviewsOwed and doctor output: legacy-unversioned instances keep the prior advisory path; versioned instances fail closed per R1; the new delivers/delivery-target spec fields use the existing declaration format. No contract migration needed.

Memo reuse only when the ancestor chain is disjoint from visited scopes, sufficient because cycle checks read only closeoutChain; equivalence with the plain verifier tested for linear, ancestor-intersecting and cyclic topologies.

Examined how the design addresses the stated cause (profile: repeated GetSpec/ArtifactResolver parse and repeated predecessor verification). D1 allocates per-operation resolver snapshots, removing repeated catalogue parses (R2, measured by the specCatalogueListed hook); D1/D2 add the bounded closeout memo for repeated terminal verification (R6). Both are confined to the audited operation, so the final audit (R1/R4) remains the correctness boundary.

No user-facing doc, template or scaffold changes are needed: doctor output is unchanged. The spec's delivery target, final report and follow-ups describe runtime behavior; the R1 trace overstatement is captured separately as low N2.
Doctor still names `pose closeout-check <scope>` when listing fails; memo limits fall back to the original verifier rather than erroring.

Compared the change set with the spec's Artifacts and non-goals: only declared implementation files changed; round 2 adds only spec/report/index/bundle governance records; no persistent cache, catalogue or policy change.

Examined authority boundaries: a dynamic Authorize disables the memo; missing/duplicate/unauthorized identities resolve identically to the live path; snapshots never cross operations; same-size/restored-mtime edits are refused by the final audit.

Compared with the smallest alternative: snapshots alone were measured insufficient (>600 s, spec execution log), so the memo is justified. It is bounded (2048 entries, 256/32768 visited), confined to one callback, keeps only approvals, and has no persistence or extension points. The choice is invalidated if closeoutChain gains other readers or terminal verification starts depending on caller state outside the guarded fields; the code comments state these limits.
